404. Existence is tested before containment: the name is joined to REPORTS_DIR, then to BASE_DIR, and when neither join exists the handler raises the not-found error and never reaches the containment check. A traversal name is therefore not rejected by a safe-path validation in this route.
403. This is the only branch that produces 403: the joined path exists and its resolved form does not satisfy the containment comparison against the resolved BASE_DIR.

Served with 200 although the file is outside the base directory. The containment check is str(filepath.resolve()).startswith(str(BASE_DIR.resolve())), a byte-prefix comparison with no path-separator or component boundary, so a resolved path such as /srv/audit-backup/sibling_report.xlsx satisfies a resolved base of /srv/audit. Recorded as observed legacy behaviour and as a containment weakness; the fixture states no target rule and no remediation.

note: Generator outcomes are injected deterministically; no external process is executed by the fixture. The two packaging failure cases are kept apart on purpose: a non-zero generator exit produces no log line at all, while an exception inside the generation block is printed and then swallowed. Both end with a complete, successfully streamed archive that is missing the report member.
download_guard_note: The three download cases exist because the route's guard is ordered existence-first and its containment test is a string prefix. DL-ESCAPE is a 404, DL-OUTSIDE is the only 403, and DL-PREFIX is served. None of the three is a safe-path validation performed before resolution.
